Title: February 12, 2026 – Boulder City Council Special Meeting

Topic1.Title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Agenda Amendment, and Consent Agenda
Topic1.Summary: Mayor Brockett called the special meeting to order and a quorum was confirmed by roll call. Council unanimously voted to remove item 6A (the assault weapons certification period discussion) from the agenda. The consent agenda items 2A and 2B were moved, seconded, and approved unanimously by roll call.

Topic2.Title: Area 3 Planning Reserve: Staff Presentation on Community Needs Assessment
Topic2.Summary: Planning staff (Brad Mueller, Sarah Horn) presented the results of Step Two of the service area expansion process for the Area 3 planning reserve. Council was asked only whether community needs are of sufficient priority to keep the door open to Step Three, the service area expansion plan, not whether to expand. Staff evaluated six needs: housing (about 9,500 units needed by 2032), a fire rescue storage facility, continuum-of-care facilities for older adults, regional parkland, small-scale farming, and renewable energy. Each was assessed against community value, capacity, and benefit. Staff noted the Planning Board voted 4-3 on Jan. 20 that the needs are not a sufficient priority at this time, and outlined three possible paths forward depending on council's vote.

Topic3.Title: Council Clarifying Questions on Area 3
Topic3.Summary: Council members questioned staff on the middle-income housing gap data, parkland standards and maintenance funding, leasing land for energy projects, and the procedures for disposing of designated parkland. They also asked about staff capacity and cost (an estimated $300–500K in consultant fees, an 18–24 month process), when to set design guardrails, phasing, and who pays for infrastructure. Water supply tradeoffs, wildfire water needs, habitat and state agricultural plans, and accessibility were also raised. Staff clarified that a yes vote would not require starting the expansion plan immediately, and that initiating it later would take affirmative votes from both council and Planning Board.

Topic4.Title: Public Hearing on Area 3 Planning Reserve
Topic4.Summary: Four speakers addressed council. Jonathan Singer of the Boulder Chamber, Adrian Sopher, and former council member Macon Cowles urged moving forward, citing the need for middle-income and missing-middle housing and the risk of delay. Lynn Segal opposed the proposal, citing water supply, wildfire, transportation congestion, and the unknowns around the Colorado River. Speakers also stressed that tonight's decision only keeps options open.

Topic5.Title: Council Deliberation and Vote on Finding of Need
Topic5.Summary: Most council members supported moving forward to preserve future flexibility and explore housing types not being built elsewhere, but several wanted guardrails such as a focus on middle-income and family housing, financial stress testing of infrastructure costs, and no new fossil fuels. Councilmember Spear raised concerns about habitat, water, and the Colorado River, and Councilmember Marquis said he would defer to the Planning Board without guardrails. Staff were directed to draft a resolution of intentions and guardrails for adoption on a future consent agenda, with hotline feedback due Feb. 19. Council then voted 7-2 (Wallach and Adams opposed) that the identified needs are of sufficient priority to warrant further consideration of a service area expansion plan.

Topic6.Title: Reconsideration of Comprehensive Plan Community Change Requests
Topic6.Summary: Staff explained that the Board of County Commissioners advanced three land use requests (7, 8, 9) and two policy requests (30, 32) that staff and the other bodies had not recommended moving forward. Staff recommended against reconsidering them, noting that the requests were inconsistent with draft policy and land use direction, and that annexation policy language is already being revised. No council member proposed reconsidering any of the requests, so no further action will be taken.

Topic7.Title: Municipal Court Update
Topic7.Summary: Presiding Judge Jeff Kahn and Court Administrator Devon Kiss-Kelly reviewed 2025 caseloads, including rising traffic and criminal filings, a record 72,000 photo enforcement citations, 72,000 parking citations, and 8,400 parking appeals. They also covered an increase in quality-of-life violations near CU, community court participation and counseling, and the launch of a public data dashboard. For 2026 they plan to enhance the dashboard, strengthen community court, and adapt to the Colorado Supreme Court's Camp decision and pending state legislation affecting public defender contracts. Council members thanked the court for its work, especially the data dashboard.

Topic8.Title: City Council Community Engagement Update and Discussion
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented a menu of 2026 council engagement options: chats with council, council-initiated chats, office hours, community connectors and residents events, and a community and council forum. Council members expressed support for continuing chats and the annual forum, and several suggested topics including bicycle security downtown, student and youth outreach, agriculture tours, and the power outage priority. Councilmember Spear suggested revisiting the rule barring candidates from chats, and the mayor pro tem asked staff to avoid labor-intensive events with low turnout. Staff will take the feedback to the engagement committee on Feb. 25, and the meeting adjourned at about 9:24 p.m.
